title: Customer pilot conclusion briefing and roadmap
content:
Executive summary:

This document summarizes the results and recommended next steps following the 6-week customer pilot ("Pilot Omega") for real-time support summarization and answer routing. The pilot validated Redwood’s hosted inference path for initial rollout under typical traffic (peak 15 rps), and identified two integration blockers for full production: (1) structured audit log formatting for compliance, and (2) a retry/fallback policy gap for long-tail token bursts.

POC goals (agreed at kickoff):
- Validate end-to-end latency under real traffic profile (<120ms p50 for single-turn generation; <350ms p95).
- Confirm cost per 1M tokens when using batching + prefix cache vs baseline.
- Verify quality: extractive summary ROUGE-L >= 0.62 vs gold set and customer satisfaction >= 4/5 on pilot reviews.
- Validate operational observability and routing policies for multi-model fallback.

Success criteria and measured outcomes:
- Latency: p50 = 92ms, p95 = 310ms (meets goal). Notable variance during token-burst windows where p95 rose to ~420ms for 30s windows.
- Cost: Observed 27% token-cost reduction using a conservative batching and prefix cache config vs the project baseline. Modeled optimized config shows potential up to 42% savings.
- Quality: ROUGE-L average 0.64; pilot reviewer CSAT = 4.2/5. Several edge cases with hallucinated entity dates occurred ~6% of outputs.
- Reliability: 99.78% uptime across pilot weeks; two incidents during autoscaling test where fallback incorrectly routed to a larger model without truncation policy, causing spikes in cost.

Key technical findings (concise):
1) Serving runtime: kernel selection and quantization profile for the chosen open encoder-decoder model performed well; memory pressure was seen only on 32k-context paths. Recommendation: limit 32k-context to dedicated capacity unless aggressive KV-summarization is applied.
2) Caching: prefix/KV cache gave measurable latency gains on repeating queries, but cache key collision with partial session IDs caused some incorrect reuse. Fix requires canonicalization of session IDs at the client or server-side normalization.
3) Routing & fallback: current policy lacks a cost-aware truncation step prior to fallback; during overload it picks larger compatible model variants, amplifying cost. Implement an intermediate truncation/condense policy.
4) Observability: token-level cost attribution and per-route latency histograms worked; however, audit log schema did not satisfy customer compliance team (missing structured event types and consistent user identifiers).

Deployment recommendation (short-term vs long-term):
- Short-term (MVP rollout, 8–12 weeks): Use Redwood Hosted API with pinned model version + conservative autoscale policy. Apply server-side session canonicalization and enable prefix caching with a TTL of 10 minutes. Add a cost-aware truncation policy that runs prior to fallback. Deploy a compliance log adapter to transform logs into the customer’s audit schema.
- Mid-term (3–6 months): Transition sensitive, high-volume tenants to Redwood Dedicated pools (reserved capacity). Dedicated pools would host 32k-context variants and isolate KV-heavy workloads.
- Long-term (6–12 months): For regulated data requirements, plan a Private deployment with customer-managed KMS and on-prem ingest gates. This aligns with contract expansion for enterprise SLAs.

Risk register and mitigations:
- Risk: Hallucinated entity dates (~6% of samples) -> Mitigation: Add targeted evals + prompt engineering; enable additional hallucination detector reranker in the pipeline.
- Risk: Cost spikes during fallback to larger model -> Mitigation: Implement truncation and cost-aware fallback; add quota enforcement and burst-limited autoscale.
- Risk: Compliance audit log mismatch -> Mitigation: Deliver audit-log adapter and integration test suite in 2 sprints; provide sample logs for customer validation.
- Risk: Session ID canonicalization requires client changes -> Mitigation: Provide server-side canonicalizer as temporary shim and a migration checklist for client teams.

Estimated incremental cost impact (MVP, monthly projections):
- Hosted MVP baseline (predicted): $5.6k/month for nominal usage profile (1M tokens/day equivalent).
- Hosted with batching & cache (observed): $4.1k/month (approx -27%).
- Worst-case fallback spikes (observed incident): up to $9k in a high-burst month if fallback triggers unbounded model selection.
Note: Dedicated pricing estimates for the same workload (reserved 16-GPU pool) ~ $26k/month but yields guaranteed p95 SLAs and reduced per-token cost at scale.

Action matrix (owners and timeline):
- Deliver audit-log adapter and sample logs -> Owner: Priya Rao; ETA: 2 weeks.
- Implement server-side session canonicalizer -> Owner: Aiden Chen; ETA: 1 sprint (2 weeks), with client migration guide.
- Add cost-aware truncation before fallback -> Owner: Eng/Serving Runtime (Samir Kaur); ETA: 3 weeks.
- Configure Dedicated sizing proposal and financial model -> Owner: Solutions Eng (Maya Patel); ETA: 1 week.
- Post-POC quality sweep & targeted eval set -> Owner: Research/Applied ML (Liam O'Connor); ETA: 2 weeks.
- Customer review & signoff meeting -> Owner: Customer Success (assigned CSM); ETA: schedule in next 7 days.

Proposed roadmap and milestones (high level):
Week 0–2: quick fixes (audit adapter, session canonicalizer shim, client checklist).
Week 3–6: deploy truncation policy, refine batching rules, run second pass stress test (simulate 25 rps bursts).
Week 7–12: MVP rollout to 2 production teams, measure SLOs, prepare Dedicated sizing if commit threshold reached.

Open questions for the customer (to resolve before production rollout):
- Which specific audit event fields are mandatory for compliance (we provided sample, need confirmation).
- Are there internal session-id or user-id transformation constraints (PII redaction rules)?
- Contract commitment threshold for Dedicated pricing: is the customer willing to commit to 6–12 months at X usage?

Appendix (artifacts and evidence):
- Per-route latency heatmap (attached in spreadsheet in Jira SE-4212).
- Example audit-log sample (json) uploaded to the pilot repo.
- Pilot evaluator notebook with ROUGE results and coffee-scripted edge-case examples.

Conclusion and recommended immediate next steps (recommended by Solutions Eng):
1) Ship audit-log adapter and session canonicalizer shim to unblock compliance signoff within 2 weeks.
2) Implement truncation policy to control cost exposure during fallback.
3) Run a targeted quality sweep and deploy a hallucination reranker for entity dates.
4) Schedule an executive readout with the customer and our GtM lead to discuss Dedicated pricing and timeline.

If we prioritize the three quick wins (audit adapter, canonicalizer shim, truncation policy) we expect the customer to be comfortable with an initial hosted MVP rollout within 8–12 weeks and be in a position to evaluate Dedicated capacity by the quarter end.

Notes to self / internal follow-ups:
- Create a short demo script showing fallback behavior before/after truncation.
- Draft contract amendment language for dedicated pool option and share with legal.
- Track pilot postmortem incident (autoscale fallback) and link remediation PRs to the incident ticket.
summary: Executive readout of Pilot Omega: met latency and quality targets overall; identified audit-log and fallback cost issues; recommended immediate fixes (audit adapter, session canonicalizer, truncation policy) and a staged plan toward Dedicated capacity.
